title: Sunny and the Cricket Choir | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka sits in the middle of a moonlit clearing and realises the crickets all around her are singing together in the most perfect, steady chorus she has ever heard. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The crickets were singing.

Sunny had always heard them — they were part of every bush night, as constant as the stars. But tonight she sat still for long enough to really listen.

There were so many of them.

Not one or two — hundreds. Thousands, maybe. Each one a tiny instrument, each one playing a different small piece of the same long note. Together they made something enormous: a sound that rose and fell and breathed, like something alive.

She turned her head slowly, listening to how the sound changed depending on which way she faced. The crickets to her left were slightly higher. The ones behind her came through the grass differently, muffled and close. The ones ahead were the clearest.

She was sitting in the middle of a choir.

The cricket sound wasn't all the same pitch, she realised. It shifted slightly. Pulsed. As if all those hundreds of tiny singers were breathing together.

She lay back in the grass.

The sound surrounded her.

She thought: this is what it means to be held by the night.

The crickets sang and sang and sang — steady as a heartbeat, soft as breath, endless as the dark sky above her.

She closed her eyes.

And the whole singing world carried her down into sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, cricket choir. Goodnight, little one.
